extracted.intended_audience: scholars and practitioners in journalism and computational journalism; newsroom managers and journalists interested in algorithmic tools and gatekeeping
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter examining how computational journalistic tools (CJTs) change the gatekeeping role of newsworkers across news distribution and audience moderation, based on expert interviews with Belgian journalists. Focuses on interaction patterns, decision-making dynamics, and consequences for audience relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing role of gatekeeping with CJTs
rubrics_metrics.description: Examines the changing role of gatekeeping of newsworkers as they interact with computational journalistic tools (CJTs) in news distribution and moderation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this dimension to evaluate how CJTs alter who decides what is news and how audience content is handled; assess shifts in responsibilities and decision authority between humans and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain of gatekeeping activity: news distribution vs audience moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: CJTs can alter how daily decisions are made in both how news is distributed and how comments of the audience are moderated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat distribution (selection, ranking, recommendation of stories) and moderation (comment filtering, removal, visibility) as distinct evaluative domains; measure CJT effects separately for each domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of CJT assistance / shared decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJTs assist the newsworker in the gatekeeping process, resulting in 'shared decision-making.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent to which CJTs suggest, filter, or make choices versus those retained by human journalists; consider workflows where decisions are collaborative between tool and human actor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation of audience relation / constructiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding the audience relation, the newsworkers mention that the connection with the audience has been transformed and has become more constructive over the years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quality of audience engagement after CJT introduction — is interaction more constructive, reciprocal, or meaningful? Look for evidence of improved dialogue or participatory practices enabled by tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience paradox (reduced direct connection when CJTs take charge)
rubrics_metrics.description: When CJTs get more in charge of the gatekeeping, an 'audience paradox' emerges, as the newsworker is less connected with the audience via these CJTs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure unintended consequences: increased automation may distance journalists from audiences even if engagement metrics rise; probe changes in journalist awareness of audience sentiment and feedback loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworker–CJT interaction frequency and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Study conducted with journalists who interact with CJTs on a weekly basis, highlighting routine interactions between newsworkers and tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how often and in what routines journalists use CJTs (daily/weekly), and how habitual use shapes gatekeeping choices and reliance on metrics or recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of audience metrics on editorial selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Cites literature on how metric data (audience clicks, reader metrics) influence news editorial selection and start a 'subtle revolution' in tracking the online audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the degree to which audience analytics and performance metrics (clicks, engagement) drive selection and placement decisions, and how CJTs operationalize those metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normative considerations about algorithmic gatekeepers
rubrics_metrics.description: Raises normative questions about what kind of news gatekeepers we want machines to be (filter bubbles, fragmentation, normative dimensions of algorithmic recommendations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate CJTs not only technically but ethically and normatively: consider risks like filter bubbles, audience fragmentation, fairness, transparency, and alignment with journalistic values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design considerations for editorial-orientation algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to design considerations for editorial orientation algorithms in journalism (how algorithms are oriented toward editorial goals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this dimension to judge whether CJTs are designed/configured to reflect editorial priorities (news values, diversity, public interest) and whether design choices are documented and auditable.
